math_errors.location: §3.2 ETA model, T_seg(ℓ) (line 51) and its use in §3.3 t_out = t_in + κ_e T_seg(ℓ_e)
math_errors.error: T_seg assumes the robot accelerates from rest and decelerates to rest on EVERY corridor segment. On a multi-segment route the robot does not stop at each vertex, so the model over-estimates by v_c/a per segment (1.5 s at v_c=1.5 m/s): for a 10 m aisle segment 8.17 s vs 6.67 s (+22 %), for 5 m 4.83 s vs 3.33 s (+45 %). This violates spec 4.4's ≤15 % ETA error target by construction, and a multiplicative per-edge κ_e cannot fix a bias that depends on whether the robot stops at that vertex or not.
math_errors.correction: Compute the speed profile over the whole granted prefix (accelerate once, cruise, decelerate only at stops/hold vertices; impose a junction/turn speed limit v_turn and add v_turn-to-v_c transitions), or equivalently add the v_c/a term only at vertices where a stop or in-place rotation is planned. Keep κ_e for residual calibration and validate against the 15 % target in S1.

math_errors.location: §3.3 safety pad δ_s = d_safe + v_max(τ_c+τ_ctrl) + ε_loc = 0.68 m (line 58)
math_errors.error: Positions p_i are base_link centres, but the pad omits the robot body (spec: 600 × 400 mm). A reference-point crossing a resource boundary leaves 0.3 m of body still inside; two robots whose reference points are 0.68 m apart have only 0.08 m between bodies, which is below the 0.3 m E-stop threshold of spec 4.7. Braking distance v²/(2a) (2 m at v_max) is also absent for hold-vertex placement.
math_errors.correction: δ_s must include L_robot (or L/2 at each of the two boundaries): δ_s = L_robot + d_safe + v_max(τ_c+τ_ctrl) + ε_loc ≈ 1.28 m. Separately require that every hold vertex lies ≥ v_approach²/(2a) + L/2 + xy_goal_tolerance before the next resource boundary.

math_errors.location: §3.3 δ_t = δ_s / v_nom with v_nom = 1.0 m/s fixed (line 58)
math_errors.error: A fixed time pad does not give a fixed spatial pad. On a narrow aisle (spec: robot width + 20 cm) robots will move at ~0.3–0.5 m/s, so 0.68 s covers only 0.2–0.34 m; at v_max = 2.0 m/s on the main corridor it covers 1.36 m (over-conservative). The unit check [m]/[m/s]=[s] is correct but the quantity chosen is not the planned speed.
math_errors.correction: Use a per-edge pad δ_t,e = δ_s / v_e with v_e the planned (speed-limited) edge speed, or the minimum expected speed on that edge.

math_errors.location: §3.3 junction occupancy interval [t_out − δ_t, t_out + T_rot + δ_t] (line 57)
math_errors.error: Treats the junction as a point: the interval contains only rotation time plus pads. A junction has the physical extent of the intersecting corridors (2–3 m on the main corridor); traversing it at 1 m/s takes 2–3 s plus L_robot/v, i.e. ~2 s more than reserved. Under-reservation of the 4-way intersection is exactly the S2 case that is supposed to be collision-free.
math_errors.correction: Model junction j with a traversal length ℓ_j (e.g. corridor width + L_robot) and reserve [t_out − δ_t, t_out + T_rot + (ℓ_j + L_robot)/v_j + δ_t]; or split junctions into node resources with explicit lengths in the geojson.

math_errors.location: §2 (line 28) 'wide corridors = two one-way lanes, cap(r)=1' vs §3.3 (line 59) 'same-direction lanes need only entry order + headway h ≥ δ_t'
math_errors.error: Contradictory capacity model: cap = 1 forbids a second robot on the lane, while the headway rule admits a platoon. The interval-overlap conflict predicate a_1<b_2 ∧ a_2<b_1 is only correct for cap = 1; with headway-following the predicate must be on entry-time differences, and the headway bound h ≥ δ_t is not derived (a follower needs h·v ≥ v·τ_react + L_robot with equal braking, and full v²/(2a) if the leader can E-stop instantly).
math_errors.correction: Either (a) model lanes as chains of short blocks of length ≥ L_robot + stopping distance, each cap = 1, or (b) give lanes cap = ⌊ℓ_e /(L_robot + d_headway)⌋ and replace the overlap predicate on those resources with an ordered entry-time predicate t_in,j − t_in,i ≥ h and t_out,j − t_out,i ≥ h, deriving h from the braking model.

math_errors.location: §3.3 SIPP transition 't' = max(t + κ_e T_e, t_w_lower) and e must be free during [t, t']' (line 60)
math_errors.error: Waiting is charged to the edge. In SIPP the wait happens at the source vertex u inside u's safe interval; the edge must be free only during the actual traversal [t' − κ_e T_e, t']. As written, a robot waiting for w's safe interval blocks corridor e for the whole wait (over-conservative), and the departure time is never checked against u's safe interval (unsafe if u is a capacity-1 junction).
math_errors.correction: t_dep = t' − κ_e T_e must lie in the current safe interval of u; require e free during [t_dep − δ_t, t' + δ_t]; if u is a resource, extend u's reservation to cover the wait.

math_errors.location: §5.1.1 item 3 definition of P and §5.1.3 Theorem 1 proof (lines 115, 139)
math_errors.error: P is defined with only inter-robot edges (consecutive reservations on the same resource), yet the proof invokes 'a robot's own resource sequence is time-monotone', i.e. intra-robot (type-1) edges. Without them 'P is a DAG' is neither necessary nor sufficient: robot i: r1→r2, robot j: r2→r1 produces inter-robot edges (i→j)_r1 and (j→i)_r2 — a 2-cycle on robot nodes — while the plan is time-feasible; conversely, the switch test of Theorem 3 on inter-robot edges alone can accept a switch that closes a cycle through type-1 edges. Theorem 1 also silently needs δ_t > 0 (or a closed-interval predicate): with δ_t = 0 the simultaneous swap through a shared vertex satisfies t ≤ t and is not excluded.
math_errors.correction: Define P on (robot, resource) events with type-1 edges (i,r_k)→(i,r_{k+1}) and type-2 edges exit(i,r)→enter(j,r); state Theorem 1 as 'strictly separated reservations (b_i ≤ a_j with δ_t > 0) ⇒ the event graph is acyclic'; run the Theorem-3 DAG check on the full event graph; require the minimum pad level in S4 to be strictly positive.

math_errors.error: (b) 'a robot that received a token for r traverses and reports exit in finite time' is circular: a robot holding r and waiting at the end of r for r' does not exit r until r' is granted, which is what the theorem is trying to prove. The correct assumption is that a granted MOVE completes in finite time and that exit(r) is the same event as enter(r').
math_errors.correction: Restate (b) as 'any move whose precedence predecessors are satisfied and whose target resource is granted completes in finite time', define exit(r_k) ≡ enter(r_{k+1}), and carry the induction over the topological order of the event graph (Hönig et al. 2019, Thm. 1).

math_errors.location: §3.4 Banker safety test (line 68) and its use in OnNewRoute 'reject; retry with lower priority' (line 134)
math_errors.error: Written as '⇔' but described as a sufficient condition; more importantly it demands that ALL remaining resources ρ_k \ h_k of robot σ(k) be simultaneously free or held by σ(1..k−1), which rejects almost every route that shares the main corridor with another robot, while Theorems 1–2 already guarantee deadlock-freedom for any time-feasible SIPP route. The retry 'with lower priority' cannot change the outcome because the test does not depend on priority — the loop never terminates. The ablation 'Banker off' (A1) therefore measures nothing well-defined.
math_errors.correction: Drop the Banker admission for SIPP routes (they are safe by Thm 1–2), or restrict it to the case it can cover — admission of a route that bypasses the reservation table (e.g. R2 reroute on a closed graph) — and then use the sequential single-unit RAS one-step-lookahead form (Reveliotis) that checks resources in route order, not all at once. Write it as '⇒' (sufficient).

math_errors.location: §3.5 priority Π_i and the no-starvation proposition (lines 72–73); §5.1.2 pseudocode (line 124)
math_errors.error: (i) The urgency term τ_ref/max(slack, τ_ref) saturates at 1 for every slack ≤ 60 s including negative slack, so it cannot rank an already-late task above one with 50 s of slack. (ii) The proposition proves that Π grows linearly with waiting, but under CTR a robot's turn at a resource is fixed by P (derived from the SIPP priority order at planning time) and the slack switch; Π only orders SIPP calls and breaks ties among robots whose predecessors have all exited. Aging therefore never re-orders an existing reservation, and the starvation-freedom claim does not apply to the mechanism actually executed.
math_errors.correction: Replace the urgency term by a non-saturating one, e.g. w1·clip((τ_ref − slack)/τ_ref, 0, 2). State exactly where Π is consumed (SIPP planning order, victim choice, tie-breaks) and re-derive the starvation bound from the event-DAG depth (bounded number of predecessors per event), or make aging an input to the switch rule.

math_errors.location: §5.1.6 'delay has no effect on safety (order preserved)' (line 148) and §7.2 latency_bridge / ReportPassage.srv (lines 225, 227)
math_errors.error: The safety claim assumes FIFO delivery. A bridge that delays each message by an independent U(20,100) ms sample reorders messages (a message sent 10 ms later can arrive 70 ms earlier). Concretely: after a slack switch (i→j)_r → (j→i)_r a grant to i for r may already be in flight (up to 100 ms), so i enters r after j has been granted r — an order violation that Theorem 3 does not cover. ReportPassage is a service and cannot be delayed by a topic-republishing bridge at all, so the exit-report leg of the claimed 2τ_c round-trip is not actually exercised.
math_errors.correction: Give every grant/revoke/report a monotone sequence number and make the bridge FIFO per channel (or reject stale seq); make a switch two-phase (revoke-ack before re-grant, or only switch resources not yet granted to i); replace ReportPassage.srv by a topic (or wrap it) so it passes through the latency bridge.

math_errors.location: §3.4 wait-for geometric condition ⟨p_j − p_i, u_i⟩ > 0 ∧ ‖p_j − p_i‖ < d_dl (line 67)
math_errors.error: A half-plane test marks any robot anywhere in front of i within d_dl (including robots beside i in a 3 m-wide main corridor or across a junction) as blocking, creating false cycles between two robots that stop for unrelated reasons and triggering R1 back-ups.
math_errors.correction: Use a cone/footprint test (|atan2(...)| < θ_dl, and lateral offset < w_robot/2 + margin) plus 'j is also stopped', and confirm against the local costmap that i's planned path is actually occupied by j.

math_errors.location: §3.1 Hungarian complexity 'N = max(n,m) = 50 ⇒ ≤ 1.25×10^5 ops ⇒ < 5 ms in pure Python' (line 45)
math_errors.error: Squaring 5×50 to 50×50 and running O(N³) is 100× more work than needed; 1.25×10^5 Python-level operations of the O(N³) Munkres inner loops is 10–30 ms in CPython, not < 5 ms, which threatens the S1 '< 10 ms' and the §7.5 '≤ 5 ms' budget line.
math_errors.correction: Implement the rectangular Hungarian (O(n²m) ≈ 1.25×10³ for 5×50) or the row-reduction variant on the n×m matrix; keep the brute-force oracle for N ≤ 7 including rectangular cases.

math_errors.error: Not measurable as defined: when CTR is active, every predicted conflict is resolved before it occurs, so the 'ground truth' of near-misses is suppressed by the intervention itself (recall is undefined, precision is trivially 0).
math_errors.correction: Define the metric on the B0/B1 baselines (predict from the same reservation table but do not intervene) or replace it with 'predicted conflicts → interventions' counts plus near-miss rate as an independent safety KPI.

math_errors.location: §6.1 utilisation U_i = T_busy/T_total with busy = MOVING/DOCKING/LOADING (line 186); §6.2 S1 10-min sliding throughput (line 184)
math_errors.error: A robot waiting for a token while assigned to a task is counted as not busy, so utilisation falls exactly when traffic management is working, conflating congestion with idleness. At λ = 30 tasks/h a 10-min window contains ~5 completions, giving ±45 % noise on the sliding throughput.
math_errors.correction: Report U_assigned (assigned to a task) and U_moving separately plus a blocked-time ratio; use a ≥30-min window or cumulative throughput with confidence intervals for the λ = 30/h condition.

proposal_verdicts.reasoning: The core mechanism — plan on a segment/corridor graph with prioritized (SIPP-style) planning, derive per-segment entry preconditions from the planned order, and let a per-robot Nav2 stack execute only the released prefix — is the tuw_multi_robot MRRP design (Binder, Beck, König, Bader, IROS 2019) and its ROS2/Nav2 port (Reicher & Bader, ARW 2025), which publishes routes 'containing preconditions when a robot is allowed to enter a segment' and integrates with Nav2 via a Route Follower plugin. Released-prefix goal extension is also the standard VDA 5050 base/horizon protocol ('the AGV shall stop at the decision point if no further nodes and edges are added to the base; master control should extend the base before the AGV reaches the decision point'), openTCS's claim()/allocate() sequential resource scheduler with single-vehicle blocks, and Open-RMF's fleet adapter that trickle-feeds waypoints to Nav2 from the traffic schedule. The slack-based re-ordering with an acyclicity check is Berndt et al.'s SADG (workshop 2020, journal version IEEE T-RO 40:1356–1372, 2023, arXiv 2312.04190) with a deadline criterion instead of cumulative completion time. So novelty item (i) 'coupling to individual Nav2 stacks via goal extension' is not new, (ii) is a variant of SADG, (iii) is engineering. The design itself is sound in outline and feasible in weeks IF the mathematical defects listed (event-graph definition, body length and junction extent in reservations, per-edge pads, lane capacity, latency-safe switch protocol) are fixed; the redundant Banker admission and the optional congestion weights should be cut. The quantitative claims '≥15 % throughput over Nav2-only' and '≤10 % loss at 100 ms latency' have no supporting estimate: with 5 robots in a 60×40 m warehouse, B0 rarely conflicts in the random 1-h scenario and pads/hold stops cost throughput, so CTR may well be slower than a non-deadlocking B0; if B0 deadlocks its throughput collapses and +15 % is trivial. Honest label: engineering_adaptation (of MRRP/ADG/SADG/VDA5050) with a real, useful contribution being the verified Nav2-Humble integration (onPreempt in navigate_through_poses.cpp updates goals without restarting the BT when the same BT file is used — I confirmed this in the Humble source).
proposal_verdicts.evidence: Reicher & Bader, 'Multi Robot Route Planning for ROS2', Austrian Robotics Workshop 2025, doi:10.34749/3061-0710.2025.19 (preconditions per segment, Nav2 Route Follower, Stage simulation); Binder et al., 'Multi Robot Route Planning (MRRP): Extended Spatial-Temporal Prioritized Planning', IROS 2019 pp. 4133–4139 (tuw_multi_robot_router publishes Route with preconditions); VDA 5050 v2.0 §6.6 base/horizon; openTCS Scheduler API (claim/allocate, SINGLE_VEHICLE_ONLY blocks); Ekumen 'Nav2 + Open-RMF' fleet adapter trickle-feed; Berndt, van Duijkeren, Palmieri, Kleiner, Keviczky, 'Receding Horizon Re-Ordering of Multi-Agent Execution Schedules', IEEE T-RO 2023 (arXiv 2312.04190); Hönig et al. RA-L 2019 ADG; navigation2/humble/nav2_bt_navigator/src/navigators/navigate_through_poses.cpp onPreempt.

proposal_verdicts.proposal: HRA — Hungarian + Regret-swap Auction under deadlines
proposal_verdicts.reasoning: Correctly positioned as variant_of_prior and the components are standard; the event-triggered n×K_t Hungarian with tardiness penalty, 2-opt regret swaps and a hysteresis θ_sw for pre-pickup reassignment are all feasible in a week. Two positioning gaps: swap-based improvement of Hungarian assignments is exactly Liu & Shell's 'anytime assignment: from local task swapping to global optimality' (Autonomous Robots 2013), and deadline-aware MAPD assignment predates Makino & Ito — Wu et al., 'Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery with Task Deadlines', SoCS 2021 — neither is cited. Congestion-aware assignment costs from traffic estimates are also in Zhang, Chen, Harabor, Le Bodic, Stuckey, 'Flow-Based Task Assignment for Large-Scale Online MAPD' (arXiv 2508.05890, Aug 2025), which is inside the brief's survey window and missing. The numeric targets are overclaimed relative to evidence: 'total distance ≤ 0.9× nearest' is asserted while the objective being optimized is time+tardiness, not distance (metric/objective mismatch), and '≥30 % fewer tardy tasks' is borrowed from V1's qualitative direction. Also, with n = 5 and K_t ≥ 10 the batch Hungarian is a one-task-per-robot matching, not a schedule, so its advantage over nearest in steady state is expected to be a few percent; state hypotheses accordingly.
proposal_verdicts.evidence: Liu & Shell, Autonomous Robots 2013, doi:10.1007/s10514-013-9351-2; Wu, Liu, Tang, Cai, Bai, Khonstantine, Zhao, SoCS 2021 (ojs.aaai.org/index.php/SOCS/article/view/18585); Zhang et al. arXiv 2508.05890; Makino & Ito arXiv 2403.12377 (verified: IROS 2024, D-TP/D-TPTS).

proposal_verdicts.proposal: Congestion-aware edge weights on the corridor graph (optional ablation)
proposal_verdicts.reasoning: Occupancy-weighted edge costs from the reservation table are the standard 'traffic-aware guidance' idea (Chen et al. AAAI 2024, Zhang et al. IJCAI 2024, Shen et al. 2026, all cited) and, for the assignment side, Zhang et al. 2508.05890. The brief already labels it engineering_adaptation and expects ≤5 % effect at 5 robots; there is nothing wrong with it, but it adds a tuning parameter μ and an ablation row to a 4-week plan that is already over-committed. Recommend dropping it from the plan (keep as a one-line future-work note) rather than spending W4 on it.
proposal_verdicts.evidence: Chen, Harabor, Li, Stuckey AAAI 2024 (arXiv 2308.11234); Zhang et al. IJCAI 2024 (arXiv 2402.01446); Zhang et al. arXiv 2508.05890 (congestion-aware edge cost model in assignment).

spec_gaps: Spec 4.8 '단일 작업 성공률 97 % 이상' is a quantitative target inside a section the brief claims to cover (§1 table row 4.8) but it appears nowhere in §6 KPIs, scenarios or targets; worse, resolver step R3 (§5.4 line 177) marks a task Failed after 3 deadlock attempts, which directly consumes the 3 % failure budget — the brief must define re-queue/re-assign instead of Failed and report success rate in S1/S5.

Spec 4.9 monitoring requires battery level and current task per robot, and the 4-hour endurance (4.10) with a charging zone in the reference layout implies charging must be scheduled; the state model x_i (§2) has no battery term, the assignment cost has no charging/return-to-charge task, and S5 does not say how robots charge. A 4-h run with simulated battery drain will stall without this.

Spec 4.9 alerts for '긴급 정지, 작업 실패, 교착': only DeadlockEvent.msg is defined (§7.2); no alert/event interface for task failure or E-stop, and the kpi_node has no published topic/message for the Foxglove/web dashboard to consume (KPI display is a spec requirement in this area).

Spec 4.4 '예측 시간 오차 15 % 이내' is invoked in §3.2 as shared, but no scenario measures ETA error (observed vs predicted per task/edge) and the per-segment stop-start model is biased beyond 15 % on 5–10 m segments (see math errors). Add an ETA-error KPI to S1/S2 with the 15 % pass criterion.

Spec 4.9 '통신 지연(최대 100 ms) 반영': the latency bridge covers topics only; ReportPassage.srv (exit reports, the very leg the safety argument depends on) and AssignTask.srv are services and bypass the bridge, so the claimed latency tolerance is not actually tested end-to-end.

Spec 4.4 narrow passage (robot width + 20 cm) vs the brief's well-formed-pocket assumption (§2 line 28, §3.4 T3): a 0.6 m-wide aisle cannot contain a pocket, in-place rotation (0.72 m diagonal) is impossible inside it, and docking + loading (spec 4.8: 5–15 s load, ArUco docking with up to 3 retries) inside an aisle holds that resource for 10–60 s. The brief neither reserves station dwell time (τ_dock + τ_load) in the reservation table nor states which stations lie on capacity-1 corridors. Specify the layout constraint explicitly and add dwell reservations.

Spec 4.8 task state machine (Pending/InProgress/Completed/Failed, events published): transitions under HRA reassignment before pickup, R2 reroute, R3 escalation and cancel are not specified; 'Failed' vs 'Pending (re-queued)' matters for the 97 % target and the dashboard.

Spec 4.10 API documentation: the four new interfaces (PassageGrant, TrafficState, DeadlockEvent, ReportPassage) are named but not specified (field units, seq numbers, QoS/latching for TrafficState), and no sequence diagram for the grant/exit/switch protocol, which the architecture document requires.

Spec 4.10 response time '명령 수신 ~ 로봇 반응' budget (§7.5) assigns 50 ms to the team's own A* first segment with no measurement; spec 4.4 allows A* replanning up to 500 ms, so the 180 ms mean is unsupported until the team's A* latency on a 960k-cell grid (or the shorter prefix goal) is measured. Add an S6 sub-measurement of each stage.
required_revisions: §5.1.1/§5.1.3: define the precedence graph P on (robot,resource) events with intra-robot (type-1) and inter-robot exit→enter (type-2) edges; restate Theorem 1 with strict separation (δ_t > 0), fix the circular assumption (b) of Theorem 2 (granted move completes in finite time; exit(r_k) ≡ enter(r_{k+1})), and run the Theorem-3 acyclicity check on the full event graph; add a unit test that the swap example (i: r1→r2, j: r2→r1) is rejected.

§3.3: rewrite the reservation geometry — include L_robot in δ_s (≈1.28 m), use per-edge δ_t,e = δ_s/v_e, give junctions a traversal length, reserve station dwell (τ_dock + τ_load) at endpoints, and fix the SIPP transition so waiting is charged to the source vertex's safe interval, not the edge.
§2/§3.3: resolve the lane-capacity contradiction (cap = 1 vs headway platooning); derive the headway h from the braking model or split lanes into cap-1 blocks.
§3.2: replace per-segment stop-start ETA with a route-level profile (stops only at hold vertices/turns, junction speed limit); add an ETA-error KPI with the spec's 15 % criterion.

§3.4/§5.1.2: remove the Banker admission from the SIPP route path (redundant with Thm 1–2, priority-independent retry loops forever) or restrict it to reroutes that bypass the reservation table and use the sequential one-step-lookahead form; delete the 'Banker off' ablation or redefine it.
§3.5: fix the saturating urgency term; state where Π is consumed (SIPP order, tie-breaks, victim choice) and re-derive starvation-freedom from the event-DAG depth, or feed aging into the switch rule.

§5.1.6/§7.2: make the grant/report protocol latency-safe — sequence numbers on grants, revokes and reports; FIFO (or seq-filtered) latency bridge; two-phase switch (revoke-ack before re-grant, or switch only ungranted resources); convert ReportPassage to a topic so it is delayed by the bridge.

§5.4: add a multi-robot yield for T1/T4 (head-on with convoys behind both sides), since single-victim BackUp/reroute cannot resolve it; replace R3 'mark task Failed' with re-queue + operator alert to protect the 97 % success target; add a livelock argument that covers alternating cycles with different robot sets.

§5.1.8 and §0: relabel CTR as engineering_adaptation; cite and position against tuw_multi_robot MRRP (Binder et al. IROS 2019) and Reicher & Bader ARW 2025 (segment preconditions + Nav2 Route Follower), VDA 5050 base/horizon release, openTCS scheduler, Open-RMF fleet-adapter trickle-feed, and the T-RO 2023 SADG journal paper (arXiv 2312.04190) instead of only the 2020 workshop version; state precisely what differs (continuous-time pads, slack criterion, Humble goal-preemption path).

§5.2: cite Wu et al. SoCS 2021 (MAPD with deadlines), Liu & Shell 2013 (swap-based anytime assignment) and Zhang et al. 2508.05890 (flow-based/congestion-aware TA); restate targets as hypotheses with the metric matching the objective (weighted tardiness primary, distance secondary, 'report the measured ratio' instead of 0.9×).

§6.2: replace '≥+15 % throughput vs B0' with 'zero deadlocks/collisions at ≤ X % throughput loss vs non-deadlocking B0, and ≥ Y % vs B1'; report S3 success with a Wilson interval (20 samples); require the minimum S4 pad level to be > 0; add S5 charging behaviour, battery KPI, task-success-rate and alert checks; add per-stage response-time measurement in S6.
§6.1: split utilisation into assigned/moving/blocked; redefine the conflict-prediction KPI on baseline logs; use ≥30-min windows at λ = 30/h.
§3.1: implement the rectangular O(n²m) Hungarian and re-measure the '< 5 ms' claim; keep the brute-force oracle.

§7.6: descope W4 — drop §5.3 congestion weights and the Banker ablation, keep the slack switch as a stretch goal, and reserve time for corridor-graph authoring, the Nav2 preemption/DWA deceleration test (open question 1) and the 4-h endurance run in sim time.

§9: add DOI-verified entries for R9 (the DOI in the structured summary, 10.1023/A:1011294320501, does not resolve; the paper is IJFMS 13:385–404, 2001) and cite the T-RO 2023 version of R13; state that the arXiv API works over https (the 429s were transient) and rerun the queries to catch 2512.09736 (Yan et al., planner trade-offs under ADG execution) and 2508.05890.
